answer: A concrete Sybil defense is edge aging in the trust graph: every vouch has a half-life and must be renewed by a fresh mutual interaction, so a farm's pre-built edges decay before they can be used. An atlas of dormant accounts loses its connections, and a cipher of stale vouches no longer unlocks weight. A thread of continuously renewed relationships is what survives, which requires ongoing honest contact. The attacker's cost is keeping every edge alive across every clone, an ongoing social expense that stockpiled identities cannot prepay.
